chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: It is not for the believer to possess knowledge without jurisprudence (understanding) in it.
Nor jurisprudence without knowledge, for indeed knowledge is by practice/action.

key_terms.عِلْم: Knowledge (general awareness or specific religious knowledge)

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between knowledge and jurisprudence in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) teaching that 'ilm is not merely intellectual accumulation but a transformative force realized through amal, establishing the epistemological foundation of Shia jurisprudence. This linkage underscores the principle that true gnosis (ma'rifah) necessitates practical adherence to divine law, distinguishing mere scholars from the truly knowledgeable who embody their learning in conduct.
